speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) given the weak economic indicators for the past several months, including rising unemployment, slower growth projections and a weak global economic outlook, whether a recession is imminent and, if so, what are some of the measures that the Government is contemplating.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Since the Global Financial Crisis, global growth has been weaker than expected and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has been downgrading its global growth forecast almost every year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In the near term, the global economic outlook is expected to remain weak.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Investment demand in key advanced economies remains sluggish, while China's growth continues to moderate as it restructures its economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Low oil prices have also affected the growth prospects of oil exporters, including those in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: At the same time, global trade flows have been weak, in part due to the sluggish global growth, as well as in-sourcing trends in economies like China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: First, externally-oriented services sectors, such as finance and insurance, and wholesale trade, have slowed and could continue to face external headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Second, although manufacturing output saw a pick-up in the second quarter, it has shown signs of weakening on the back of sluggish external demand.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Low oil prices have continued to dampen the performance of firms in the marine and offshore engineering segment, as well as those in the precision engineering cluster that support the global oil and gas industry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In line with the weakness seen in the manufacturing sector, non-oil domestic exports (NODX) contracted over the July to August period.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Third, domestically-oriented sectors, such as food services and real estate, are likely to remain weak.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Notwithstanding the general slowdown in growth, there are bright spots in the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Tourism-related sectors, such as accommodation, have benefited from the recovery in tourist arrivals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Growth in "other services industries" and the information and communications sector is also expected to remain resilient, supported by growth in the education, health and social services, as well as the IT and information services segments respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: MTI will be releasing the advance estimates of third quarter GDP growth on 14 October and the updated growth forecast for 2016 in November.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Depending on the nature and severity of the downturn, the Government is prepared to consider introducing a range of contingency measures, which could include broad-based as well as sector-specific measures.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Companies adversely affected by the slowdown can tap on assistance measures that are already put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Given the sluggish economic conditions and domestic restructuring, unemployment and redundancies have risen slightly.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Government will work with our tripartite partners to step up efforts to help our displaced workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These include various career and employment support schemes under SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Minister Lim Swee Say will be elaborating on these efforts later on.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Despite the global headwinds, it is important that we press on with our efforts to steer our economy towards a more sustainable growth path driven by productivity and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We must continue to transform our industries and create good jobs for Singaporeans over the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Minister Iswaran will be elaborating on some of the efforts in these areas as well.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Given the sombre outlook and from my chat with my friends in various businesses, I think the outlook is one of great uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There seems to be very few spots of positive news.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And from the consumers' side, looking at the various reports, consumer confidence is at an all-time low.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, when I put these two together, for many of us, we feel that a recession is imminent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My question to the Minister is: do we wait for that to come or do we try to put some measures in place to forestall these dark clouds that I see coming?

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: But, overall, we expect our economy to still grow at between 1% and 2%, albeit on the lower end of the projection.
